# Settings reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/dev/gen-settings-reference.py — do not edit; edit its sources and run it again. -->

Every setting the Runway kernel and its essential protection plugin read: what it does, the values it takes, and where you set it. Per-site settings are made on the site console's screens (SITE-MANAGER-GUIDE.md); optional plugins document their own settings.

## How settings are layered

- **The console** keeps what you set on its screens in `external/platform.yml` (platform) and in each site's folder (that site). Only values that differ from the default are stored. A blank field restores the default; a blank token field keeps the stored token.
- **The server** can set any key in `external/application.yml`, an environment variable (`RUNWAY_CSP_MODE` for `runway.csp.mode`) or a command-line argument. **A value set there wins**, and the console shows that field disabled with where it is set, and what removing it there would do. To move a key to the console in one restart, click **Use the file's value** on its row first (it copies the value the server runs with), then remove the line and restart: nothing changes (ADMINISTRATION.md §8).
  Two exceptions. *Password strength* (`runway.security.password-strength`): the value chosen on Platform settings wins over every server source, and the field is never locked. *The protection plugin's settings* (section 2): `external/plugin-settings/protection.yml`, which its settings screen writes, wins over `external/application.yml`, and the form shows no lock; an environment variable or a command-line argument still wins over both.
- **When a change applies:** the settings in section 1 apply after the next restart (the form says which are pending). Settings on the other screens in section 2 say when they apply.
- **Kept out of the console on purpose:** the settings in section 3, each with the reason.

## 1. Console settings: Server settings and the policy cards

### Settings → Server settings

Screen: `/__app/config/server` (platform administrators). Applies after a restart.

#### Content-Security-Policy

The browser security policy every page is sent with. It limits where scripts, styles, images and frames may come from. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `runway.csp.mode` | report sends the policy as report-only (violations are logged, nothing is blocked); enforce blocks what the policy does not allow; off sends no policy. | one of `report`, `enforce`, `off`; default `report` |
| Use strict-dynamic (master switch) | `runway.csp.strict-dynamic` | A script the page loaded with its nonce may load further scripts. On: console pages use it, and public pages too while the switch below is on. Off rolls every page, console and public, back to the host lists below. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Use strict-dynamic on public pages | `runway.csp.public-strict-dynamic` | Public pages get a nonce and strict-dynamic too. Needs the switch above. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Extra allowed hosts (all sites) | `runway.csp.extra-hosts` | Every site's pages may load from these hosts, e.g. https://www.youtube.com. They are added to scripts, styles, images, fonts, connections and frames. For a host only one site needs, use Settings → Embed hosts instead. | comma-separated list; default empty |
| Upgrade insecure requests | `runway.csp.upgrade-insecure-requests` | The browser fetches http:// resources over https:// instead. | `true` or `false`; default `false` |
| Report URI *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.report-uri` | Where browsers send violation reports. The default is Runway's own collector, which writes them to the log. A blank field restores this default; to send no reports at all, set runway.csp.report-uri: "" in external/application.yml. | text; default `/__csp-report` |
| default-src *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.default-src` | The source list for anything without its own directive. A blank field restores 'self'; to leave the directive out, set the key to "" in external/application.yml. | text; default `'self'` |
| script-src *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.script-src` | Script sources. The page's nonce (and strict-dynamic, when on) is always added. | text; default `'self'` |
| style-src *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.style-src` | Style sources. | text; default `'self' 'unsafe-inline'` |
| img-src *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.img-src` | Image sources. | text; default `'self' data:` |
| font-src *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.font-src` | Font sources. | text; default `'self'` |
| connect-src *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.connect-src` | Where scripts may connect (fetch, XHR, WebSocket). | text; default `'self'` |
| base-uri *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.base-uri` | Allowed values of a page's <base> element. | text; default `'self'` |
| form-action *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.form-action` | Where forms may submit. | text; default `'self'` |
| frame-ancestors *(Advanced)* | `runway.csp.frame-ancestors` | Which sites may show these pages in a frame. 'none' forbids all. | text; default `'self'` |

#### Request limits

How large a request may be. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Largest request before sign-in (bytes) | `runway.endpoints.max-form-bytes` | The most a visitor who is not signed in may send in one request, on any path. Default 262144 (256 KiB). | whole number from 1024 to 104857600; default `262144` |
| Slowest request body (bytes per second) *(Advanced)* | `runway.http.min-request-data-rate` | A request body arriving more slowly is answered 408 Request Timeout, so a client sending a byte now and then cannot hold a request thread. Measured on what has arrived since the body's first byte. Default 4096; 0 turns the check off. | whole number from 0 to 1048576; default `4096` |
| Largest request to a plugin (bytes) | `runway.endpoints.max-body-bytes` | The most a signed-in user may send to a plugin's route. Default 10485760 (10 MiB). | whole number from 1024 to 1073741824; default `10485760` |
| Largest uploaded file | `spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size` | For uploads such as a backup to restore. A size like 256MB or 1GB. Default 256MB. | text; default `256MB` |
| Largest upload request | `spring.servlet.multipart.max-request-size` | All the files of one upload together. A size like 256MB. Default 256MB. | text; default `256MB` |

#### Site storage

How much each site may keep in its static files and documents. A site's own limit, set on Sites, wins over this default. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Storage per site (bytes) | `runway.static-files.default-max-bytes` | The most a site's static files and documents may take on disk. An upload that would go over it is refused; nothing already stored is deleted or hidden, and a site over it can still delete. 0: no limit. Default 0. | whole number from 0 to 9223372036854775807; default `0` |

#### HTTP caching

The Cache-Control header pages and files are sent with. A page's own cache setting in the page editor wins over these. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public pages | `runway.http-cache.public-pages` | Default: browsers and caches keep a page 5 minutes and may serve it 1 more minute while refreshing. | text; default `public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=60` |
| Site files | `runway.http-cache.assets` | Files under a site's /static/ (except the immutable kinds below). Default: one day. | text; default `public, max-age=86400` |
| Plugin files | `runway.http-cache.plugin-assets` | Files plugins serve under /__plugin/ (their styles and scripts). Default: one hour, then checked against the file's content. | text; default `public, max-age=3600` |
| Immutable file types | `runway.http-cache.immutable-extensions` | Extensions served as never changing (fonts by default). Give such files a new name when they change. | comma-separated list; default `woff2,woff,ttf,otf,eot` |
| Immutable files *(Advanced)* | `runway.http-cache.immutable-assets` | The header for the types above. Default: one year, immutable. | text; default `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` |

#### Response compression (tuning)

Fine-tuning for the compression switches above. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Smallest body to gzip (bytes) | `runway.compression.gzip.min-size` | Default 1024. | whole number from 0 to 10485760; default `1024` |
| Smallest body to Brotli-encode (bytes) | `runway.compression.brotli.min-size` | Default 1024. | whole number from 0 to 10485760; default `1024` |
| Brotli quality | `runway.compression.brotli.quality` | 0 is fastest, 11 smallest; 4 to 6 suit compressing on the fly. Default 5. | whole number from 0 to 11; default `5` |
| Largest body to compress (bytes) *(Advanced)* | `runway.compression.max-buffer-bytes` | Larger responses are sent uncompressed. Default 4194304 (4 MiB). | whole number from 65536 to 268435456; default `4194304` |
| Compressed content types *(Advanced)* | `runway.compression.mime-types` | The whole list: what you enter replaces it. | comma-separated list; default `text/html,text/xml,text/plain,text/css,text/javascript,application/javascript,application/json,application/xml,image/svg+xml` |

#### Monitoring

The health probe each site answers at /__health, the metrics endpoint, and the site reload endpoint. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Answer the health probe (/__health) | `runway.health.enabled` | Off: /__health is not served. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Check the site's content too | `runway.health.content-check` | The probe also checks that the home page and the master template are there. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Content check result kept for (seconds) *(Advanced)* | `runway.health.content-check-ttl-seconds` | Default 10. | whole number from 1 to 3600; default `10` |
| Health detail token | `runway.health.token` | A probe that sends it as a Bearer token gets the detailed body. Never set: only the public answer. A blank field keeps the stored token; type a new one to replace it. | secret (stored encrypted, never shown); default empty |
| Metrics scrape token | `runway.metrics.scrape-token` | Lets a monitoring system read /actuator/prometheus with this Bearer token. Never set: only signed-in operators can. A blank field keeps the stored token; type a new one to replace it. | secret (stored encrypted, never shown); default empty |
| Site reload endpoint | `runway.reload.enabled` | Lets a deployment script make a site re-read its files. Inactive until the token is set. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Reload token | `runway.reload.token` | The Bearer token the reload endpoint requires. A blank field keeps the stored token; type a new one to replace it. | secret (stored encrypted, never shown); default empty |

#### Site logs

The access and audit log each site keeps (its Logs and Insights screens). Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Keep site logs | `runway.logs.enabled` | Off: no site records new access or audit lines; the Logs screen keeps the lines already written, Insights shows nothing. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Longest a site may keep its logs (days) | `runway.logs.max-retention-days` | Each site chooses its own retention up to this. Default 90. | whole number from 1 to 3650; default `90` |
| Record the browser (User-Agent) | `runway.logs.access-log-user-agent` | Adds the User-Agent to each access line. | `true` or `false`; default `false` |
| Log queue size (lines) *(Advanced)* | `runway.logs.queue-capacity` | Lines waiting to be written; beyond it lines are dropped and counted. Default 8192. | whole number from 16 to 1048576; default `8192` |

#### Console languages

The languages this console's language switcher offers. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Languages offered | `runway.operator.ui-languages` | Language codes in display order. Each needs a console translation: en and es ship, others go in external/i18n/. | comma-separated list; default `en,es` |
| Default language | `runway.operator.default-language` | Used when the browser asks for none of the languages offered. | text; default `en` |

#### Sessions

How long a signed-in console session lasts without activity. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle session timeout | `server.servlet.session.timeout` | A duration such as 30m, 2h or 1d. Default 30m. | text; default `30m` |

#### Reverse proxy

Whether to trust X-Forwarded-* headers, and from which addresses. Only from your own proxy: otherwise visitors could fake their address. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Read X-Forwarded-* headers | `runway.proxy.forwarded-headers` | From the trusted addresses below only. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Trusted proxy addresses | `runway.proxy.trusted-cidrs` | The exact address of your reverse proxy, e.g. 10.0.0.5/32, and of every proxy in front of it (a CDN). Check the result under About Runway → This request. A /0 (0.0.0.0/0, ::/0), or ranges that add up to every address (0.0.0.0/1 with 128.0.0.0/1), would trust every client to fake its address, so it is refused. | comma-separated list; default `127.0.0.1/32,::1/128` |

#### Capacity

Threads and concurrency limits. The defaults suit most servers; raise them only for measured load. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Most request threads | `server.jetty.threads.max` | Default 200. | whole number from 8 to 10000; default `200` |
| Fewest request threads *(Advanced)* | `server.jetty.threads.min` | Default 8; never above the most. | whole number from 1 to 1000; default `8` |
| Message file re-check (seconds) *(Advanced)* | `runway.i18n.cache-seconds` | How often a site's message files are checked for changes made outside the console (Messages screen saves apply at once). 0: on every use. Default 5. | whole number from 0 to 3600; default `5` |
| Scheduler threads *(Advanced)* | `spring.task.scheduling.pool.size` | Threads for backups and plugin jobs. Default 4. | whole number from 1 to 64; default `4` |
| Password checks at once *(Advanced)* | `runway.security.max-concurrent-hashes` | Each takes about 19 MiB (32 MiB with the High profile). Beyond it, sign-ins wait. Default 8. | whole number from 1 to 256; default `8` |
| Longest wait for a password check (ms) *(Advanced)* | `runway.security.acquire-timeout-millis` | Then the sign-in answers "busy". Default 2000. | whole number from 100 to 60000; default `2000` |

#### Protection logging

What the request protection writes to the log when it refuses a request. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Log refused requests | `runway.protect.log-rejections` | One line per refused request (403 or 429). The count in the metrics is kept either way. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Repeat lines suppressed for (seconds) | `runway.protect.log-rejection-window-seconds` | For the same address and reason; the next line says how many were suppressed. Default 60. | whole number from 1 to 86400; default `60` |

### Backups → Settings (backup policy)

Screen: `/__app/config/backups` (platform administrators). Applies after a restart.

#### Backup policy

Automatic backups of every site, and how many stored backups are kept. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Back up every site automatically | `runway.backups.schedule.enabled` | On the schedule below. | `true` or `false`; default `false` |
| Schedule | `runway.backups.schedule.cron` | Six fields: second minute hour day month weekday. Default 0 30 2 * * * (02:30 every day). | text; default `0 30 2 * * *` |
| Stored backups kept per site | `runway.backups.retention.max-count` | The newest this many are kept; 0 keeps all. Default 30. | whole number from 0 to 100000; default `30` |
| Delete stored backups older than (days) | `runway.backups.retention.max-age-days` | 0: no age limit. Default 0. | whole number from 0 to 36500; default `0` |
| Largest file inside a backup to restore (bytes) *(Advanced)* | `runway.backups.max-entry-bytes` | A guard against archives that expand without limit. Default 268435456 (256 MiB). | whole number from 1048576 to 17179869184; default `268435456` |

### Bandwidth → Settings (metering and quota)

Screen: `/__app/config/bandwidth` (platform administrators). Applies after a restart.

#### Metering and quota

Per-site traffic counting, its history, and the monthly cap. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Count each site's traffic | `runway.bandwidth.enabled` | Off: nothing new is counted and no cap is enforced; the Bandwidth screens keep the history already recorded. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Monthly cap per site (bytes) | `runway.bandwidth.quota.default-monthly-bytes` | Outbound bytes in the last 30 days; above it the site's public pages answer 503 (its console keeps working). 0: no cap. A site's own cap is set on Sites. | whole number from 0 to 9223372036854775807; default `0` |
| Keep traffic history (days) | `runway.bandwidth.retention-days` | Default 90. | whole number from 1 to 3650; default `90` |
| Counting interval (seconds) *(Advanced)* | `runway.bandwidth.snapshot-seconds` | Also how often the cap is checked. Default 60. | whole number from 1 to 3600; default `60` |

### Activity → Logs → Settings (activity log retention)

Screen: `/__app/config/activity` (platform administrators). Applies after a restart.

#### Activity log

How long the console's activity log is kept. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Keep the activity log (days) | `runway.app-activity.retention-days` | Default 90. Switching the log off is set on the server only, so it cannot be done by the people it records. | whole number from 1 to 3650; default `90` |

### Plugins → Settings (plugin limits)

Screen: `/__app/config/plugins` (platform administrators). Applies after a restart.

#### Plugin limits

Size limits for installing plugins and for the files plugins keep per site. Applies after a restart.

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Largest file inside a plugin to install (bytes) | `runway.plugins.max-entry-bytes` | Default 134217728 (128 MiB). | whole number from 1048576 to 4294967296; default `134217728` |
| Largest file a plugin keeps per site (bytes) | `runway.plugins.site-files.max-write-bytes` | Default 16777216 (16 MiB). | whole number from 1024 to 1073741824; default `16777216` |

## 2. Settings edited on other console screens

| Key | Where |
|---|---|
| `runway.compression.enabled` | Settings → Platform settings, Response compression (applies at once) |
| `runway.compression.brotli.enabled` | Settings → Platform settings, Response compression (applies at once) |
| `runway.compression.gzip.enabled` | Settings → Platform settings, Response compression (applies at once) |
| `runway.node.name` | Settings → Platform settings, Node name (the console's value wins over this key) |
| `runway.security.password-strength` | Settings → Platform settings, Password strength (applies to new passwords after a restart; the console's value wins over this key) |
| `runway.bandwidth.quota.per-site` | Sites → Edit, Monthly bandwidth cap, per site (applies at once) |

Log levels (`logging.level.<logger>`) are set on **Activity → Logs → Log levels** (`/__app/logs/levels`): they apply at once and are kept in `platform.yml`; a level set in `application.yml` wins and shows locked.

The essential protection plugin's settings are on **Plugins → Essential Protection → Settings** (`/__app/plugins/protection/settings`). They are stored in `external/plugin-settings/protection.yml` and bound as `runway.plugin.protection.<key>`; they apply after a restart. Its login protection (honeypot, lockout, CAPTCHA) is the panel below that form and applies at once; each site has its own on `/__admin/protection`.

#### Rate limit

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rate-limit burst capacity | `runway.plugin.protection.rate-limit.capacity` | How many requests one address may make back to back before it is slowed down. Default 120. | whole number from 1 to 100000; default `120` |
| Rate-limit refill per second | `runway.plugin.protection.rate-limit.refill-per-second` | How many requests per second an address gets back after a burst. Default 2; 0.5 means one every two seconds. Must be above 0. | number from 0.01 to 10000; default `2` |

#### Auto-block

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auto-block repeat offenders | `runway.plugin.protection.rate-limit.auto-block.enabled` | Off: an address over the limit only gets 429s and is never blocked. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Auto-block after this many rate-limit breaches | `runway.plugin.protection.rate-limit.auto-block.breach-threshold` | How many 429s within the window before the address is blocked. Default 60. | whole number from 1 to 100000; default `60` |
| Counted within (seconds) | `runway.plugin.protection.rate-limit.auto-block.window-seconds` | The period the 429s are counted over. Default 60 seconds. | whole number from 1 to 86400; default `60` |
| Auto-block duration (seconds) | `runway.plugin.protection.rate-limit.auto-block.block-seconds` | How long an auto-block lasts; the visitor gets 429 with the remaining time in Retry-After. Default 900 (15 minutes). | whole number from 1 to 604800; default `900` |

#### Exemptions

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Never rate-limit or auto-block these IPs/CIDRs (your own audits, probes, load tests) | `runway.plugin.protection.allowlist` | One IP or CIDR per line, e.g. 203.0.113.7 or 198.51.100.0/24. For your own audits, probes and load tests. Loopback is not exempt unless listed: behind a same-host proxy every visitor arrives from loopback. | comma-separated list; default empty |

#### Remember this device

| Setting | Key | What it does | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| Allow "remember this device" (skip the login captcha on trusted devices) | `runway.plugin.protection.remember-device.enabled` | Off: the login CAPTCHA is shown on every login. | `true` or `false`; default `true` |
| Remember a device for (days) | `runway.plugin.protection.remember-device.days` | How long a device is remembered, 1 to 365. Default 30. | whole number from 1 to 365; default `30` |

## 3. Server-only settings, and why

Set these in `external/application.yml` (or the environment). They stay out of the console because the console cannot change them safely, or cannot exist until they are known.

| Keys | Why not in the console |
|---|---|
| `runway.app-activity.enabled` | It switches off the operator activity log. If the console could turn it off, an operator could silence the record of their own actions. |
| `runway.backups.offsite-dir` | A folder on the server that receives full site archives (user records, encrypted plugin secrets). Set from a browser it could point into a web-served folder or another site's folder; choosing and mounting the share is the server administrator's job. Shown read-only on Backups. |
| `runway.cluster.enabled`<br>`runway.cluster.cluster-name`<br>`runway.cluster.topology`<br>`runway.cluster.session-ttl`<br>`runway.cluster.sessions-map-name`<br>`runway.cluster.events-topic-name`<br>`runway.cluster.embedded.discovery`<br>`runway.cluster.embedded.members`<br>`runway.cluster.embedded.port`<br>`runway.cluster.embedded.port-auto-increment`<br>`runway.cluster.client.addresses`<br>`runway.cluster.client.smart-routing` | Read before the application is built (the cluster member and the shared session store are created at startup), and every node must hold the same value; one node's console cannot change the others. |
| `runway.console.hosts` | The host names the operator console answers on. A wrong value would lock every operator out of the console, so the console cannot be the place to change it: the file on the server is the way back in. Read at startup; each node of a cluster reads its own. |
| `runway.demo.first-run.id`<br>`runway.demo.first-run.host`<br>`runway.demo.first-run.master-username`<br>`runway.demo.first-run.master-password` | Used once, on the first start of an unattended evaluation box, before any operator exists to sign in. The console equivalent is Sites → Install a demo site. |
| `runway.plugins.root` | Read before the application starts: the plugin loader finds the plugins there before the console exists, and the folder decides what code the server runs. |
| `runway.security.app-master-id` | The trust anchor that pins the undeletable application superadmin, read before the application starts; set by the setup wizard and never edited by hand. |
| `runway.security.secret-key` | The key that encrypts every other stored secret. Typing it into a browser would put it on the wire, and changing it would make every stored secret unreadable; the installer keeps it in a root-only file. |
| `runway.storage.external`<br>`runway.storage.sites` | Read before the application starts: the data folder holds application.yml, platform.yml and every site, so the console cannot live anywhere until it is known. |
| `runway.storage.backups` | Read before the application starts, like the data folder, and it receives full site archives (the same reason as runway.backups.offsite-dir). |
| `runway.storage.stats`<br>`runway.storage.logs` | Retired before 1.0 and has no effect; a value set in application.yml is reported once at startup. |
| `runway.tls.enabled`<br>`runway.tls.keystore`<br>`runway.tls.keystore-password`<br>`runway.tls.keystore-type`<br>`runway.tls.key-alias`<br>`runway.tls.sni-host-check`<br>`runway.tls.watch-keystore`<br>`runway.tls.redirect-http.enabled`<br>`runway.tls.redirect-http.port`<br>`runway.tls.redirect-http.status`<br>`runway.tls.redirect-http.acme-challenges-dir` | Read before the server starts serving: the HTTPS and redirect listeners are built from it at startup, and a wrong value set from the console could make the console itself unreachable. The certificate files and their password belong to the server. |

Spring Boot keys Runway pins in its shipped `application.yml` (for example `server.forward-headers-strategy`, `spring.web.resources.add-mappings`, `spring.security.filter.order`) are part of how the platform works, not preferences: do not change them. ADMINISTRATION.md §8 lists them.
